h1: Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel — River-View Rooms on the Chao Phraya in the Heart of Chai Nat
intro: Chai Nat doesn't offer a long list of hotels, and if you want to wake up, open the curtains and find the Chao Phraya River drifting past your window, Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel is the first name locals mention · A 3-star riverside hotel in the middle of town — easy to reach, with its own riverside Thai restaurant, a buffet breakfast guests keep bringing up, and free parking · Rooms start from about THB 700/night for a standard small-building room, up to river-view suites in the main building.

River-view room with a private balcony looking out over the Chao Phraya River

body.html: Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel opened around 2014 at 1013 Moo 4, Ban Kluai, Mueang Chai Nat — right on the bank of the Chao Phraya River, yet still inside the town, just a few minutes' drive from markets, restaurants and government offices · That's a rare combination in Chai Nat, giving you both a river view and the convenience of town in one spot, which is why people here for work or breaking a journey north tend to pick it.

Rooms split into two main zones — the main building facing the river, and a small building at friendlier prices · River-view rooms come with a private balcony to sit out and catch the breeze, the feature guests love most · Standard rooms run around 22–24 sq m with air conditioning, satellite TV, a fridge and minibar, and hot water · To be straight about it, the rooms aren't new and the design is fairly plain, but they're spacious enough and the beds are comfortable.
"Opened the curtains in the morning to the Chao Phraya flowing right past the room, sipped coffee on the quiet balcony — great value for Chai Nat."

The genuine standout guests mention again and again is the buffet breakfast and the riverside Thai restaurant, Chom Bua · Bold home-style Thai dishes eaten with the river right there, especially lovely in the evening · Many reviews say the food is better than expected for a provincial hotel, and it's a reason locals drop by to eat even when they aren't staying.

Another distinctive touch is the hotel's own Chao Phraya river-cruise packages, starting around THB 890 · A nice low-key evening activity, drifting past riverside life in Chai Nat · There's free parking on site, which matters a lot if you're driving yourself, plus meeting rooms for seminars — making it a popular choice for training sessions and functions in the province.

The honest caveats — there's no swimming pool, and the building and bathrooms are showing their age · Some reviews flag bathroom cleanliness and minor maintenance issues · If you're expecting a brand-new hotel or resort-style facilities, this isn't it; but judged on its riverside location, food and price, it's fair value for what you get.

In short, Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel suits anyone who wants to stay by the river in central Chai Nat at an easy-to-reach price · An overall score of about 7.8 from real reviews across platforms reflects exactly that — strong location and food, rooms that are fine but not luxurious · Book a river-view room in the main building and don't mind the dated rooms, and most guests come away happy.

honestSummary: Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel is the best riverside option in central Chai Nat for travelers who want a river view, good food and accessible pricing · The trade-off is accepting that the building and bathrooms are aging, and there's no swimming pool.
honestChecks: If you genuinely want a river view — be sure to book a main-building room facing the river → small-building rooms are cheaper but have no water view.
If you expect a brand-new hotel or a pool — this place leans on location and food rather than luxury; rooms are plain and aging → set your expectations before booking.
If you come on a weekend or during a seminar — rooms and the restaurant can fill up, as locals favour it for functions → book ahead and pick a free-cancellation rate.

tips.title: Specify a main-building river-view room
tips.body: When booking, ask for a main-building room facing the river — small-building rooms are cheaper but have no water view. Request a higher floor for an open view.

tips.title: Have dinner at the riverside restaurant
tips.body: Chom Bua is best around sunset. Order river fish or tom yum and enjoy the cool evening over the water.

tips.title: Try the river-cruise package
tips.body: The hotel runs Chao Phraya cruises from about THB 890 — ask at the front desk. A nice low-key evening activity.

tips.title: Visit Chai Nat Bird Park
tips.body: It's a short drive from the hotel and the province's headline attraction. Go in the morning before the heat.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel, Chai Nat

faq.q: Where is Chaophayathara Riverside Hotel in Chai Nat?
faq.a: It's at 1013 Moo 4, Ban Kluai, Mueang District, Chai Nat, right on the Chao Phraya River yet still in town · About 5 minutes' drive to markets and Wat Phra Borommathat, and ~15 minutes to Chai Nat Bird Park and the Chao Phraya Dam.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from about THB 700/night for a small-building Standard room · Deluxe River View runs around THB 1,100 and a river-view Suite around THB 1,600 · Prices vary by season and package, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Which rooms have a Chao Phraya river view?
faq.a: You need a main-building room facing the river, which comes with a private balcony · Small-building rooms are cheaper but have no water view, so specify 'River View' clearly when you book.

faq.q: Is there a pool and parking?
faq.a: There is no swimming pool, but there is free on-site parking · The hotel has the riverside Chom Bua Thai restaurant, meeting rooms, and Chao Phraya river-cruise packages.

faq.q: What are the breakfast and restaurant like?
faq.a: Breakfast is a buffet that's frequently praised in reviews · The riverside Chom Bua restaurant serves bold Thai food and is lovely in the evening — locals drop by to eat even without staying.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone wanting to stay by the river in central Chai Nat at an accessible price · Travelers breaking a journey, people here for work, or visitors to Chai Nat Bird Park · Less suited to those wanting a luxury resort with a pool.
